description:
FOUND s470bz (Opus, 2026-09-07) while proving the #1302 root resolver: every
process that loads tools/lib/PCLProc.pm emits two lines on stderr AT COMPILE
TIME, before doing anything:

    Statement unlikely to be reached at tools/lib/PCLProc.pm line 58.
            (Maybe you meant system() when you said exec()?)

Reproduce: `perl -c tools/lib/PCLProc.pm`, or just run
`perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl --no-gate perl-tests/loopctl.t 2>&1 | head -2`.
Present on b5e9f845 and on every tree since PCLProc landed (#367), so it is old
noise, not a regression.

CAUSE, run_isolated (PCLProc.pm:56-59):

    exec('/bin/sh', '-c', $cmd);
    POSIX::_exit(127);

The `_exit` is a deliberate belt for a failing exec, and perl warns because a
statement after exec is normally dead code.  perl's own documented spelling of
"I meant it" is to make the fallback the RHS of an operator:

    exec('/bin/sh', '-c', $cmd) or POSIX::_exit(127);

WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO FILE: the sweep and the companion runner both load
this module, so two lines of unrelated warning sit at the top of every one of
their stderr captures.  This project compares runner stderr byte for byte (the
RUNNERS row of CLAUDE.md's WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table, and the #339 drop
announcement is read out of exactly that stream); noise there is the thing
those comparisons have to be taught to ignore.

NOT FIXED HERE deliberately: it is a runner change, so it owes the RUNNERS
row's full bar (one sweep, verdicts compared file by file), and s470bz was
already paying that bar for a different change â mixing the two would have made
neither attributable.
subject: tools/lib/PCLProc.pm:58 prints "Statement unlikely to be reached" on the stderr of every sweep and companion run
